answer: A quartz clock makes sybil identities expensive in time, not just money. To register, an agent must complete a sequential verifiable-delay puzzle tuned to a quartz oscillator's steady tick: it cannot be parallelized, so one attacker spawning a thousand fake agents must pay a thousand sequential waits, while an honest agent pays the wait only once. Each finished ticket is then mirrored into a public lantern ledger where peers can inspect and challenge duplicates, and any identity caught mirroring another's ticket forfeits its bond. Time becomes the scarce resource.
